title: release: attach .nupkg artifacts to GitHub Releases
body:
## Summary

`scripts/create-github-release.mjs` and `.github/workflows/release.yml` create
the GitHub Release but never attach the `.nupkg` files produced by
`dotnet pack`. As a result, the release on GitHub is text-only and consumers
have to go to nuget.org for the actual artifacts. The user-facing requirement
of "deploy to NuGet in GitHub Releases" is only half-implemented.

Reproduced downstream in
[link-foundation/link-cli#79](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/issues/79).

## Reproduction

1. Run any release path that calls `scripts/create-github-release.mjs`
   (auto, instant, or changeset-PR mode).
2. Open the resulting release on GitHub.
3. Observe that the `Assets` section only lists the auto-generated source
   archives — no `.nupkg` is attached, even though `dotnet pack` produced one
   and the workflow's `nuget push` step already uploaded it.

## Suggested fix

Pass the artifact glob into `create-github-release.mjs` and have the script
upload the matching files via `gh release upload --clobber` after creating the
release. The downstream PR shows the change applied to a fork of the script:

- Add a `--assets-glob` CLI flag.
- After the release is created (or already exists), resolve the glob to a list
  of files and call `gh release upload <tag> <files...> --clobber --repo <repo>`.
- Wire `--assets-glob "csharp/artifacts/*.nupkg"` (or the template's actual
  `./artifacts/*.nupkg` path) into both the auto release job and the instant
  release job.

The downstream patch lives in
[link-foundation/link-cli PR #81](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/81)
and includes a unit test that exercises the `--assets-glob` flag with a
`--dry-run`, so it can be ported back without surprises.

## Workaround

Add a manual `gh release upload "${TAG}" ./artifacts/*.nupkg --clobber` step to
the workflow after the release is created, until the script supports it.
